result.topic_en: Latin notes on the case n = 2 of the heat-conduction prize problem, in which u is not composed of finitely many terms of the form f(t)e^{λt}; Riemann reduces the conditions on u to a heat equation and adds side calculations for the case n = 1 in two variables.
result.transcription:
Jam disquisitiones ad [-casu-] casum $n=2$ vertimus, et quidem casu, in quo $u$ non est conflatum e numero finito terminorum formae $f(t)e^{\lambda t}$. Tum $u$ habet formam $u=\alpha\varphi(\beta,t)+\psi(\beta,t)$ et praeter aequationem $\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\alpha^2}=0$ habentur duae:
1. $B\frac{\partial^2u}{\partial\beta^2}+C\frac{\partial^2u}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}+D\frac{\partial u}{\partial\alpha}+E\frac{\partial u}{\partial\beta}=0$
2.) $[-A(u)-]=B_1\frac{\partial^2u}{\partial\beta^2}+C_1\frac{\partial^2u}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}+D_1\frac{\partial u}{\partial\alpha}+E_1\frac{\partial u}{\partial\beta}=\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$
Jam si in prima earum $B$ non evanescit ex [-aequationibus-] {+expressionibus+} $\Delta(u),\Delta\Delta(u),\Delta^3(u),\Delta^4(u)$ quae sunt aequales $\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$
$\frac{\partial^2u}{\partial t^2}$ $\frac{\partial^3u}{\partial t^3}$ $\frac{\partial^4u}{\partial t^4}$ omnes quotientes differentiales praeter $\frac{\partial^2u}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}$ $\frac{\partial u}{\partial\alpha}$ $\frac{\partial u}{\partial\beta}$ ope aequationis 1. ejici possunt
unde sequitur $u$ conflatum esse e numero finito terminorum formae $f(t)e^{\lambda t}$, et quidem [-...-]
[-exponentium functionum $f(t)$-] numerus terminorum omnino tres superare non potest, {+quod+} contra hypothesin.
Et quum $B$ in aequatione 1. evanescere nequit, nisi $u$ est functio unius variabilis, aequatio 1. formam
habet:
$\frac{\partial^2u}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}=A\frac{\partial u}{\partial\alpha}+B\frac{\partial u}{\partial\beta}$ $\qquad\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial\beta}=A\varphi+\alpha\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial\beta}+B\frac{\partial\psi}{\partial\beta}$
Jam ponendo pro $\alpha$ valores speciales et eliminando $\frac{\partial\psi}{\partial\beta}$ prodit aequatio formae $\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial\beta}=m\varphi$, in qua $m$ est functio
solius $\beta$, unde sequitur, denotante $p$ functionem solius $\beta$, $\tau$ solius $t$, $\varphi$ habere formam $\tau p\tau$[?]. Tum
introducendo loco $\alpha$ novam variabilem $p\alpha$ $u$ induit formam $\alpha\tau+\psi(\beta,t)$ et habemus aequationes:
3. $\frac{\partial^2u}{\partial\alpha^2}=0$ 4. $\frac{\partial^2u}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}=0$ 5.) $\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}=A\frac{\partial^2u}{\partial\beta^2}+B\frac{\partial u}{\partial\beta}+C\frac{\partial u}{\partial\alpha}$
differentiando hanc ultimam aequationem secundum $\alpha$ et $\beta$ prodit:
$0=\frac{\partial^2A}{\partial\alpha^2}\frac{\partial^2u}{\partial\beta^2}+\frac{\partial^2B}{\partial\alpha^2}\frac{\partial u}{\partial\beta}+\frac{\partial^2C}{\partial\alpha^2}\frac{\partial u}{\partial\alpha}$ or[?]
unde concludimus $A$ $B$ $C$ esse functiones lineares ipsius $\alpha$. (Alioquin haberetur aequatio tertia inter $\frac{\partial^2u}{\partial\beta^2}$ etc. [-...-]
contra hyp.) Hinc deinde:
$0=\frac{\partial A}{\partial\alpha}\frac{\partial^3u}{\partial\beta^3}+\left(\frac{\partial^2A}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}+\frac{\partial B}{\partial\alpha}\right)\frac{\partial^2u}{\partial\beta^2}+\frac{\partial^2B}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}\frac{\partial u}{\partial\beta}+\frac{\partial^2C}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}\frac{\partial u}{\partial\alpha}$
Si {+autem+} [-enim-] $\frac{\partial A}{\partial\alpha}$ non est $=0$ ope hujus aequationis e $\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$ $\frac{\partial^2u}{\partial t^2}$ $\frac{\partial^3u}{\partial t^3}$ $\frac{\partial^4u}{\partial t^4}$ omnes quotientes differentiales praeter $\frac{\partial^2u}{\partial\beta^2}$
$\frac{\partial u}{\partial\beta}$ $\frac{\partial u}{\partial\alpha}$ ejici possunt et ut supra $u$ conflatum est e numero finito terminorum formae $f(t)e^{\lambda t}$.
Habemus itaque $\frac{\partial A}{\partial\alpha}=0$ [-...-] $\frac{\partial B}{\partial\alpha}=0$ $\frac{\partial^2C}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}=0$. unde $A$ $B$ sunt functiones solius $\beta$ $C$ est formae
$\lambda(\alpha+p)$ in qua $\lambda$ est constans et $p$ functio solius $\beta$. At introducendo loco $\alpha$ novam variabilem $\alpha+p$
efficitur [-est-] ut sit $C=\lambda\alpha$. Unde
6.) $\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}=A\frac{\partial^2u}{\partial\beta^2}+B\frac{\partial u}{\partial\beta}+\lambda\alpha\frac{\partial u}{\partial\alpha}$
Quae sponte in has duas dissolvitur:
$\frac{\partial\tau}{\partial t}=\lambda\tau$ $\qquad\frac{\partial\psi}{\partial t}=A\frac{\partial^2\psi}{\partial\beta^2}+B\frac{\partial\psi}{\partial\beta}$ $\qquad\tau=e^{\lambda t}$
Jam quum aequatio 6 esse debet transformata ζ[?] hujus:
$\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}=\frac{\partial^2u}{\partial x^2}+\frac{\partial^2u}{\partial y^2}+\frac{\partial^2u}{\partial z^2}$
facile patet functionem $\psi(\beta,t)$ et ipsam ζ[?] huic aequationi satisfacere et perinde in casu modo tractato
esse contentam.

methods.what: Form of the solution when u is linear in α
Two auxiliary linear PDEs satisfied by u
Elimination argument: iterating the operator Δ and using equation 1 to show u would be a finite sum of terms f(t)e^{λt}
methods.quote: ex [-aequationibus-] {+expressionibus+} $\Delta(u),\Delta\Delta(u),\Delta^3(u),\Delta^4(u)$ quae sunt aequales $\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$

methods.what: Differentiating equation 5 in α to show the coefficients are linear in α
Splitting of equation 6 into an ODE for τ and a 1D parabolic equation for ψ
Change of variables in the area element

items.quote:
unde sequitur $u$ conflatum esse e numero finito terminorum formae $f(t)e^{\lambda t}$, et quidem [-...-]
[-exponentium functionum $f(t)$-] numerus terminorum omnino tres superare non potest, {+quod+} contra hypothesin.
items.english: from which it follows that u is composed of a finite number of terms of the form f(t)e^{λt}, and indeed the number of terms cannot exceed three at all, which is against the hypothesis.

items.quote: unde concludimus $A$ $B$ $C$ esse functiones lineares ipsius $\alpha$.
items.english: whence we conclude that A, B, C are linear functions of α.

items.quote:

esse contentam.
items.english: it is easily seen that the function ψ(β,t) and ζ itself satisfy this equation and are likewise contained in the case just treated.

items.quote:
Quaestionis generalioris, quibusnam in casibus temperatura praeter tempus a duabus variabilibus pendere
possit, casum $n=1$ plane persolvere possumus.
items.english: Of the more general question, in which cases the temperature can depend, besides time, on two variables, we can completely solve the case n = 1.
